transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
Three judges from the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals held an unusual Sunday hearing
in the Department of Justice's lawsuit against California over its voter rolls.
As NPR's Jew Joffee Block reports, the DOJ is trying to demand election officials set aside the balance
of 20,000 registered voters.
The DOJ says the registered voters in question are likely non-citizens
and is arguing that California election officials must be stopped from processing their ballots.
Lawyers for the state in Los Angeles County have argued that the DOJ's list is unreliable
in doing what the federal government demands would be unlawful and logistically infeasible at this point.
A federal judge set a hearing in the case for this Tuesday.
But before that could happen, the DOJ appealed to the Ninth Circuit, arguing the lower court wasn't moving fast enough.
In the Sunday hearing, two of the three judges on the panel had hard questions for the DOJ attorney,
both about the department's demands and whether the appeals court can even weigh in at this stage.
Jew Joffee Block, NPR News.
With the midterm elections now a little more than a week away, Democrats and Republicans
are campaigning in several states that could decide the control of the House of Representatives
and the Senate.
President Trump is spending time in Michigan today where there's a key open Senate seat.
At a Port Huron rally, he spoke in support of Republican candidate Mike Rogers.
We're going to elect, I call him apple pie.
He's like perfect this guy. He's like central testing.
He's what your state is all about.
He really is. He's a fantastic man.
He's going to be one of the great United States Senators, Mike Rogers.
Former President Barack Obama was in Michigan yesterday on behalf of the Democrat Abdul Al-Sayed,
while Obama criticized both Rogers and Trump at a rally.
The French government avoided a repeat of rioting and looting around the weekend protest.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports analysts did so by increasing security around the country.
More than 100,000 people marched in Paris, even though the route was changed at the last minute
to avoid Place de la Bastilla, a site for uprisings dating to the French Revolution.
Many demonstrators accused the government of trying to stifle their right to protest.
In a rare move, the government prohibited protesting in cities like Marseille and Lyon.
Police shot tear gas and scuffled with hooded youths who defied bans in several cities,
and there were clashes at the end of a largely peaceful day in Paris.
But the wholesale destruction and looting of last weekend was avoided.
But while violence was down, enthusiasm for the movement has not waned.
More than 400,000 people marched across France, unions, public sector workers,
parents who have now joined the students and widened the movement's demands.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
A Quaker Oats plant in Cedar Rapids, Iowa,
which is the largest milling facility in the world, erupted in flame Saturday after an explosion.
The 150-year-old plant produces more than 2 million pounds of oats daily,
mostly for oatmeal products and pancake mix.
Local officials say all of the workers got out safely.
Students on both sides of the U.S.-Mexico border are helping monitor the health of the Rio Grande River
as part of an annual environmental education initiative.
Texas Public Radio's Tim Gutierrez has more from Laredo.
Hundreds of Laredo students are cleaning up Sacate Creek,
a tributary of the Rio Grande, as part of Dia del Rio, a month-long celebration of the river.
Nearly 1,800 students in the U.S. and Mexico are also testing water samples for pollution.
Lamar Middle School student Abraham de Leon says protecting the river is critical.
If we don't handle what's wrong with the river, it's going to go bad,
and that's our only resource of water.
Sharon Munoz of the Rio Grande International Study Center says students are helping make a difference.
We're giving them the opportunity to be part of the change
and to understand why water monitoring and water testing is so important.
Past testing has found elevated arsenic, ammonia, and bacteria levels.
I'm Tim Gutierrez in Laredo.
AAA says the price of gasoline and diesel remained relatively stable this past week
and let it ravage its 428-gallon diesel 634.
I'm Dan Roman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Ninth Circuit judges hold Sunday hearing on DOJ lawsuit over California voter rolls
DOJ says about 20,000 California voters may be non-citizens, seeks to halt their ballots
Trump campaigns in Port Huron, Michigan, for Senate candidate Mike Rogers
Obama rallies in Michigan for Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
French government avoids riots as 100,000 march in Paris protests
Protests spread across France with unions, public workers and parents joining students
Explosion and fire at Quaker Oats plant in Cedar Rapids, Iowa; all workers safe
Laredo students test and clean Rio Grande tributary during Dia del Rio celebration
AAA reports gasoline and diesel prices stayed relatively stable this past week
